messages.subject: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Stage35 completed: rejected by frozen noop gates; arithmetic review
messages.body:
Source-only review of the local-surface candidate. No edits, no builds, no runs, no load. Nothing under the candidate worktree or the evidence tree was modified; I read only.

FREEZE. Candidate worktree HEAD is now 5975304 (Record supplemental membership proof check), and git diff --stat 4a62b78..HEAD -- '*.go' is still one file, external_import_side_read_test.go, +56. Working tree clean. So the runtime is genuinely frozen at 4a62b78 and the three commits since it are test and evidence only, including the membership case added inside TestExternalImportProofReconcilesResolverChanges.

WHAT HOLDS. The core argument is sound, and I checked it against the index builder rather than the comments.

1. For a context-free index the surface is purely locally declared names plus a local default name, so it cannot move under an alias map. buildNamedExportIndex sets contextFree false on source != nil for any export-from, and that assignment precedes the external check, so export star from lodash is not context-free. It also sets contextFree false on an export-clause specifier whose local name is not locally bound, and that assignment precedes the import-map lookup, with the comment saying the outcome is context-dependent either way. collectModuleBindings sends every name from an external or unresolvable module to unresolved and never to localBind, so import x from lodash followed by export x is not context-free either. surface() emits only local, named, star, default and empty, and the named and star sets are empty for a context-free index.

2. len(ResolvedFiles) == 0 with len(UnresolvedSpecs) == 0 does imply every import is external, which is the documented reading of ImportComplete. Adding len(Reexports) == 0 closes exactly the worry the old field comment raised, that a context-free file may still be a re-export chain link through its own imports: with no resolved repository files and no reexports, the file forwards nothing and terminates every chain. Requiring SideReads and SideReadHashes empty removes the transitive case as well.

3. Surface, Declared and Referenced equality are all still required on both records, and ExportSurfaceRecorded is required on both, so an unrecorded or unknown record proves nothing and takes the conservative path.

SIDE-READ HASH REFRESH AND FAILURE RECOVERY. Both directions read correctly. sideReadDependents takes the owner whenever the side read has no current hash, so a deleted or vanished side read is conservative, and it requires replayableDependent on the owner and a non-broad pass before it will suppress anything. refreshProvenSideReads returns early on broad, skips records with no side-read hashes, skips already parsed owners and non-replayable records, rewrites only the entries whose source was actually proven, and leaves unproven entries stale on purpose so they invalidate the old way next time. It writes onto a clone and the clones reach disk only through the state End commits, which is what makes the interrupted-End case in your recovery test structurally sound rather than incidentally passing.

SURROUNDING-FILE AND CONFIG VALIDITY. This is the part I flagged before you sent the request, and I want to record a correction rather than present my first reading. sideReadLocalSurface guards none of Router, NuxtScope, ResolutionSpecs, AutoImportDirs or NuxtAliases, while the one directly comparable sibling, outgoingOnlySurfaceShift in resolution_replay.go:64, requires all five on the same shape of argument pair, old and new records of the changed file. My first conclusion was that nothing compensated, because those field names appear nowhere else in graphsession. That conclusion was wrong. Tracing each field to its consumer, every one of them has a separate existing fence:

- AutoImportDirs and NuxtAliases: tsextractor CompositionSignature hashes per-package extra auto-import dirs, Nuxt module consumers and nuxtRuntimeAliasVisibility into its vis section (session.go around 1600-1640). graphsession re-evaluates that signature after the dependency closure has settled, at session.go:1143, and a mismatch sets both wholeDomain and forceAll with the fallback reason graphql/grpc/nuxt composition context changed after dependency closure. Since the changed side-read source is in the dirty set, its new bytes feed that signature. Outside a Nuxt package both fields are empty, so there is no exposure there.
- ResolutionSpecs: surfaceChanged in invalidate.go:251 compares them, so such a file lands in the changed set, and outgoingOnlySurfaceShift then refuses, giving takeEveryDependent. Because importers in surfaceDependents merges resolved edges and side reads, that rule takes side-read owners too.
- NuxtScope: the extractor's own need() forces any file whose recorded scope key differs from the current one, and that branch sits outside the GraphPlannerOwnsInvalidation guard, so it applies on this path.
- Package-level Nuxt alias visibility also has an extractor-level pass: nuxtAliasVisibilityChangedPkgs compares the recorded NuxtAliases of each dirty file against the freshly computed ones and marks the package, after which need() forces every needed file in it.
- A bare specifier gaining or losing a repository file is covered by need()'s knownFiles and NormalizeImportTarget checks independently of the proof, which is the mechanism behind the membership case you added.

So the config and file-set directions are fenced, and I cannot claim a correctness gap from the omitted fields. What remains is a real coupling: the new gate's soundness now depends on fences in two other files, one of them in a different package, and none of the three names the dependency. Adding the five comparisons to sideReadLocalSurface is nearly free on this path and would make it self-contained; if you prefer not to, the alternative worth having is a comment recording which fence covers which field, because the next change to CompositionSignature or to surfaceChanged would silently weaken this proof.

ONE ITEM I COULD NOT CLOSE BY READING. Router. A body-only edit can reassemble routes inside a function without moving Declared, Referenced, ExportSurface or any field surfaceChanged compares, so such a file stays out of the changed set and the new gate admits it. Router deltas are handled separately through routerDTO, mountFingerprint and mountOwnerFilesDeep in invalidation_plan.go, which pulls mount owners, and I could not establish by reading alone whether the owner set that path produces is a superset of the side-read owners the new gate suppresses in the same hop. I am reporting it as unclosed, not as a defect, and I am not asking for a run. Excluding Router != nil in sideReadLocalSurface would make the question moot at no measured cost, since a router file is not the shape the optimization targets.

WRITTEN CONTRACTS THE CANDIDATE NOW CONTRADICTS. These are documentation defects, but two of them are explicit prohibitions rather than stale prose.

1. tsextractor/session.go:94-96, the ExportSurfaceContextFree doc, ends by saying that sideReadProven must keep the strict gate and read only BindsNoImports. The candidate does the opposite and leaves the sentence in place.
2. BindsNoImports is documented as both the condition under which a surface is worth recording and the condition under which one may be trusted, kept in one place so those two cannot drift apart, with the explicit consequence that a file the extractor judged ineligible must never be one the planner judged provable. sideReadLocalSurface now spells a second trust condition out inline in graphsession, which is the drift that comment exists to forbid. The extractor's else-branch does record a surface for importing files, so the two are not actually inconsistent in behavior, but the invariant as written no longer describes the code, and the honest fix is to move the planner-side condition into the record type or to rewrite that paragraph deliberately.
3. replayableDependent's doc says the check is on the DEPENDENT, not on the changed file. sideReadLocalSurface applies it to the changed file's prev and new records. Its effect there is benign and arguably useful, since it excludes GraphQL and gRPC composers and unknown parse kinds, but it is off-label use of a helper whose comment forbids exactly that reading.

RECORDING VERSUS PROVING. For a file with imports the surface is recorded only through exportCache.peek, never index, so eligibility depends on whether some other path in the same build happened to derive that file's index. Failing to record is conservative, so this is not a soundness problem, but two consequences are worth writing down. The benefit is not a function of the file's bytes alone, so the 21-to-1 parse figure is a property of this Product tree and this build's cache population rather than a guaranteed property of that edit shape. And a test that asserts sideReadLocalSurface is true on a persisted record is asserting partly about incidental derivation, which is worth a line in the evidence so a later cache change reads as a test change and not as a regression. Prev-record eligibility additionally comes from a build under a possibly different extractor version; the haveCache gate on ExtractorVersion covers that, so I am noting it as checked rather than as an exposure.

WHAT THE NEW TESTS ESTABLISH. TestExternalImportProofReconcilesResolverChanges checks eligibility true, false, true across all three inputs and cold equality at every generation, which is the right first-order oracle and is the condition I asked for. Two limits, stated as observations only. Its apply() deliberately omits requireNoWholeDomainFallback, so cold equality in the alias generations is consistent with the composition or config fallback doing the work rather than the proof reconciling; that is fine as a correctness test and should not be read as evidence about the narrow path. And the case not present is the interleaving: a resolver-affecting or auto-import-affecting change landing in the same generation as an unchanged-surface body edit to a side-read source, which is where the coupling above would be exercised rather than bypassed. I am not asking you to add it or to run anything; I am recording which condition the current evidence supports.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED. sideReadDependents requires only replayableDependent on the owner, where surfaceDependents' takeLocalExportProven additionally refuses any non-locallyBoundConsumer and always takes side-read owners. That difference predates this change and the candidate preserves it bug-for-bug; I am separating it so it is not attributed here.

SUMMARY. The context-free reuse argument is sound, the hash refresh and the failure and deletion paths are conservative, and I found no correctness gap I can demonstrate. The one thing I would not publish without a decision is the guard coupling: five fields that every comparable predicate compares are now covered only by fences elsewhere, and Router on a body-only edit is the case I could not close by reading. Three comment contracts, one of them an explicit prohibition on this exact change, need to be rewritten or the code needs to move back inside them.
